cards.body:
## Summary
The chores-uat rider re-implements the proving core's money rules four times (cap, resume, dump, report) and gets ADR 0122 wrong in all four: an unpriced leg costs $0, so `--cap-usd` never binds on a run of failing legs, a resumed run forgets them, and a dump or report prints $0.00 for spend nobody priced. Move the reading into the core's run log once and make the rider use it.

## Description
`runlog.py` gains `Spend` (spent_usd, calls, unpriced_calls, enforced_usd) and `spend(rows, assume_usd)`, plus `RunLog.read(path)`, the one tolerant JSONL reader. `Rig.spent()` returns a Spend over its rows with `assume_usd=UNPRICED_CALL_USD[CLAUDE]` (the chores legs run on the claude CLI); `run_pairs` stops scheduling on `spent_before.enforced_usd + rig.spent().enforced_usd >= cap_usd`; `ledger_spent` becomes `spend(RunLog.read(path))`. A dump's cost is the known sum or absent, with `unpriced_legs` beside it. The report header says known spend and the unpriced count, and the files go out with TEXT_ERRORS like the core's `write_report`. Technique: cost-metering/budget-enforcement (every path that starts spend points at the same check) and the core's own 'absent is omitted, never 0' rule.

## Flow
- leg finishes -> TapLedger row (cost_usd may be None) -> RunLog
- scheduler asks rig.spent() -> Spend.enforced_usd counts unpriced at $0.50 -> cap compared
- resume -> RunLog.read(ledger.jsonl) -> spend() -> spent_before (Spend, not float)
- dump/report -> Spend.spent_usd (known) + unpriced_calls, never a coerced 0

## Expected impact
A $400 subscription run whose CLI starts timing out stops at the cap instead of burning every remaining pair; the report a person reads no longer calls unpriced spend free; a lone surrogate in a judge's voice can no longer lose the report of a paid run. The bench's open twin finding (playbooks bench cap ignores unpriced turns) gets a reader it can adopt.

## Evaluation
Claim: the chores-uat cap, resume, dumps and report follow ADR 0122 and the absent-not-0 rule through one core reader.
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass (cases 3-7 fail on today's code; 1-2 have no function)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
cards.evidence: grep -n 'cost_usd") or 0' src/athena/proving/chores_uat/*.py -> report.py:158, rig.py:95, run.py:355, run.py:530, run.py:689 (five sites, one rule, none weighs unpriced). budget.py:94-97 _enforced = spent + unpriced*UNPRICED_CALL_USD (ADR 0122: '1000 unpriced charges: can_spend True, spent 0.0' was the bug it fixed for roles). chores_uat/report.py:308 md.write_text(report_md(...), encoding="utf-8") vs core report.py:72 errors=TEXT_ERRORS, and test_roles_and_budget.py:282 pins the core's surrogate case. Stabilize 2026-10-16 built 'An unpriced or failed role call costs nothing in the purse' for Budget only (675b36f); the rider (added later, ADR 0132) never got it.

cards.body:
## Summary
The chores UAT exists to certify a fix wave, and its verdict is a before/after. Today the operator compiles that delta by hand from two report.md files and has to remember, in prose, that the judge instrument moved underneath it. Add `report --against <run-id>`: the tool matches pairs, computes the deltas, lists the flips, and marks every judge-derived number as mixed when an identity key of the instrument moved.

## Description
New `chores_uat/compare.py`: `compare(base_dir, head_dir)` loads both runs' dumps and run.json, matches on pair id, and answers a document: matched n, only-in-each lists, criteria pass/fail/not-evaluable before/after with per-pair flips (null transitions counted apart, never as passes), adopt shift and changed pairs, findings by type/dimension before/after, judge-independent brief metrics ('(my guess)' lines, 'Dates that matter' sections), known cost each side, and `instrument_moved` from the same `_IDENTITY` keys the resume refusal uses (git_head informational; an absent run.json is 'unknown' and mixed). `compare_md` renders it worst-flip first. `__main__` gains `report --against`. Techniques: eval-harness/comparison-modes ('every plotted point carries its instrument versions, and any instrument change is a marked discontinuity') and eval-harness/measurement-revision (a re-run is a second sample: name n and the matched set).

## Flow
- operator lands a fix, runs `run --pairs <touched>` into a new run id
- `report --run-id HEAD --against BASE` -> compare.md: header 'over 20 matched pairs; instrument moved: judge_system -> judge deltas mixed'
- flips table: pairs that lost a criterion first, then gains; adopt changes; brief metrics (not mixed)
- the B-C item's acceptance is read off compare.json instead of a hand table

## Expected impact
The recertify step every BACKLOG B-C item waits on goes from a hand-built table to one command, and a delta confounded by an instrument change can no longer be read as a product gain (it is labelled at the number, not in a paragraph). Losses hidden inside an unchanged total (one criterion up, one down) become visible per pair.

## Evaluation
Claim: two chores-uat runs can be compared by the tool, over matched pairs, with instrument confounds marked.
Before: 0 of 7 non-guard acceptance cases pass (no compare exists)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
